- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean or 1–2 points if spike occurred.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp drop or volatility, reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 units per day.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overcorrects downward; apply “overshoot correction” by adding 1–3 points to forecast to avoid premature reversal.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% or 1–3 points to align with mean reversion behavior.
- If true outcome deviates >3% from model in first 5–7 days, apply “lag correction”: shift forecast down by 0.5–1.0 units per day for next 3–5 days to account for delayed reaction.
- For 30-day horizon, if model is flat or trending down while sentiment is positive, force a slight upward bias (0.5–1.5%) to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85–87), reduce forecast slope and add 0.5–1.0 units to avoid overestimating recovery.
